strings.heroEyebrow: One index for the whole American art world
strings.heroTitleEnd: — from the field to a single work.
strings.heroLede: Everything that usually lives in separate tabs and closed inboxes: artists and collectors, public commissions, residencies, and a live map of the museums, galleries and biennials that hold it all.

strings.audienceTitle: Join as an artist, a collector or an institution
strings.audArtistDesc: A portfolio, plus the open calls and residencies that actually fit your practice.
strings.audCollectorDesc: Provenance and title, early discovery, and a way to follow practices — not just names.
strings.audInstitutionDesc: Post a call, and appear on the atlas.
strings.sec1Title: Artists and collectors, on the same map.
strings.sec1Lede: The gap is structural, not personal. Artists can't see who is collecting; collectors can't see who is emerging until someone else decides they should.
strings.artistsPoleTitle: What the market hides from you.
strings.collectorsPoleTitle: What you need before you buy.
strings.sec2Title: Commissions — the work that gets funded.
strings.sec2Lede: Most listings bury the question that actually matters: can you apply at all? Here it's the first thing you see.
strings.sec3Title: Residencies — time, space, and a room to think.
strings.sec3Lede: What is actually provided: duration, what's funded, what you pay for, and who the door is open to.
strings.sec4Title: A map of museums, galleries and biennials.
strings.sec4Lede: Every institution as a point of light on real geography. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, search to fly.
strings.joinLede: One account connects your practice, your collection or your programme to everything else on the map. No fee to be listed.
strings.joinErr: Enter a valid email to request access.
strings.joinOk: Request received — we'll place you on the map shortly.
strings.footTagline: One index connecting artists to the industry — resolving the field from cosmos to atom.
strings.disclaimer: Every institution, residency and commission listed here is real and was checked against primary sources. Even so: programmes change, funding changes, and application windows move every year. This is not an application portal — always confirm current terms with the organisation directly using the source link on each card.

commissions.name: Percent for Art
commissions.summary: New York City sets aside a share of eligible city-funded construction budgets for permanent public artwork in libraries, schools, firehouses and parks.
commissions.budgetNote: A percentage of each eligible capital project, so it varies widely; covers design, fabrication and installation.
commissions.cycleNote: No deadlines. Artists join the Percent for Art Artist Registry on an ongoing basis, and the department draws from it to invite proposals for specific projects.

commissions.name: Chicago Percent-for-Art
commissions.org: Dept. of Cultural Affairs and Special Events
commissions.summary: City ordinance allocates 1.33% of qualifying capital project budgets to public art, one of the higher percentages among US programmes.
commissions.budgetNote: 1.33% of qualifying capital construction budgets, by city ordinance.
commissions.cycleNote: The city maintains an Artist Email Registry to announce calls, plus a prequalified list used to select artists for specific projects.

commissions.name: Percent for Art
commissions.summary: Philadelphia pioneered percent-for-art in the United States in 1959; the model has since spread to more than 350 programmes nationwide.
commissions.budgetNote: A set share of eligible capital budgets, varying by project.
commissions.cycleNote: Projects are announced individually rather than on one annual cycle. Confirm the current route with the city.

commissions.name: High Line Plinth
commissions.org: High Line Art, Friends of the High Line
commissions.summary: A dedicated pedestal on the High Line's Spur given over to a single major new sculpture, on view for 18 months at a time.
commissions.budgetNote: Commissioned, fabricated and installed by High Line Art; per-commission figures are not published.
commissions.cycleNote: Not an open call. An advisory committee nominates artists, who are invited to propose; a shortlist is shown publicly before two commissions are selected per cycle.

commissions.name: Midnight Moment
commissions.summary: A monthly moving-image commission shown simultaneously on more than 90 Times Square billboards every night from 11.57pm to midnight.
commissions.budgetNote: Screen time is donated by billboard operators, so the programme covers an artist fee and technical preparation. No submission fee.
commissions.cycleNote: Rolling open call with no fixed deadline. Proposals are accepted year-round and a new artist is programmed each month.

commissions.name: Art in Public Places
commissions.org: City of Austin Cultural Arts Division
commissions.summary: Austin commissions permanent public artwork for civic sites through a competitive public process open to artists.
commissions.budgetNote: Project budgets are published per call and vary by site.
commissions.cycleNote: Calls are issued per project through the year as RFQs or RFPs rather than on a single annual deadline.

commissions.name: One Percent for Art
commissions.summary: Kansas City commissions artwork for civic construction projects through an open, competitive process.
commissions.budgetNote: One percent of eligible capital project budgets.
commissions.cycleNote: Calls for artists are issued per project as an RFQ or RFP; there is no single annual deadline.

commissions.name: Public Art Program
commissions.summary: Seattle runs one of the longer-established municipal public art programmes in the US, commissioning work for civic sites across the city.
commissions.budgetNote: A share of eligible capital budgets; figures vary by project. Confirm with the office.
commissions.cycleNote: The office maintains artist rosters and issues project-specific calls. Confirm the current route directly.

commissions.name: Public Art Program
commissions.summary: Los Angeles commissions public artwork for civic sites and through private development requirements across the city.
commissions.budgetNote: Varies by project and funding route. Confirm with the department.
commissions.cycleNote: Opportunities are announced per project rather than on one annual cycle. Confirm the current route with DCA.

commissions.name: CIFO Grants and Commissions Program
commissions.summary: Grants and commissions supporting Latin American artists, with awards for both emerging and mid-career practitioners.
commissions.budgetNote: Award values are published per cycle and differ between the grant and commission tracks.
commissions.cycleNote: An open call run in cycles; eligibility is tied to Latin American origin. Check the foundation for the current cycle.

residencies.name: MacDowell
residencies.funding: Fully funded: private studio, meals, accommodation, and need-based stipends. No fee to attend.
residencies.disciplines: Visual art, writing, music, film, architecture, theatre
residencies.summary: The oldest artist residency in the United States, giving fellows a private studio in the woods and uninterrupted time to work.
residencies.applicationNote: Open application in cycles across disciplines, assessed by rotating peer panels. Check the current deadline on the site.

residencies.name: Yaddo
residencies.funding: Funded: room, studio and meals provided. No residency fee.
residencies.disciplines: Visual art, writing, music, film, performance
residencies.summary: A historic artists' community on a Gilded Age estate, offering long stretches of uninterrupted working time.
residencies.applicationNote: Competitive open application reviewed by peer panels, with cycles through the year.

residencies.name: Skowhegan School of Painting & Sculpture
residencies.funding: Need-based financial aid; intensive summer programme with studios and visiting faculty.
residencies.summary: A nine-week summer residency in rural Maine built around an intense peer community and visiting-artist critiques.
residencies.applicationNote: Annual application for the summer session; highly competitive.

residencies.name: Headlands Center for the Arts
residencies.funding: Artist in Residence awards include studio, housing, meals and a stipend.
residencies.disciplines: Visual art, writing, dance, music, interdisciplinary
residencies.summary: Studios in former military buildings in the Marin Headlands, just across the Golden Gate from San Francisco.
residencies.applicationNote: Annual open call for the Artist in Residence programme. Check current eligibility and dates.

residencies.name: Vermont Studio Center
residencies.funding: Fee-based with a substantial fellowship programme; fellowships cover some or all costs.
residencies.summary: The largest international residency programme in the US by number of artists hosted each year, on a riverside campus.
residencies.applicationNote: Rolling applications with fellowship deadlines through the year.

residencies.name: Djerassi Resident Artists Program
residencies.funding: Fully funded: housing, studio and meals, with no residency fee.
residencies.disciplines: Visual art, writing, music, choreography, media
residencies.summary: A residency on 580 acres of ranch land in the Santa Cruz Mountains, with outdoor sculpture sited across the property.
residencies.applicationNote: Annual open application for the following season.

residencies.name: Bemis Center for Contemporary Arts
residencies.funding: Funded: live/work studio, monthly stipend and travel support.
residencies.summary: A long-running Midwest residency with large live/work studios and a dedicated sound art programme.
residencies.applicationNote: Annual international open call reviewed by a jury.

residencies.name: Anderson Ranch Arts Center
residencies.funding: Mix of funded fellowships and fee-based places; confirm current terms.
residencies.summary: A mountain campus combining workshops with residencies and strong technical facilities.
residencies.applicationNote: Applications open annually for residency sessions.

residencies.name: Pilchuck Glass School
residencies.funding: Residency and scholarship routes; confirm what is covered for your session.
residencies.summary: The leading glass school in the United States, with a rural campus north of Seattle and a dedicated artist residency.
residencies.applicationNote: Applications run annually ahead of the summer sessions.

residencies.name: Fountainhead Residency
residencies.funding: Housing and studio provided; artists meet their own travel and material costs.
residencies.summary: A Miami residency built around connecting visiting artists to local collectors, curators and institutions.
residencies.applicationNote: Applications are reviewed on a cycle; confirm the current route with the programme.

residencies.name: Recess
residencies.funding: Session artists receive an honorarium, space and production support.
residencies.summary: A New York organisation whose Session programme turns the gallery into a public studio where work is made in view of visitors.
residencies.applicationNote: Open calls are announced per cycle rather than on a fixed annual date.

residencies.name: Penland School of Craft
residencies.funding: Resident artists receive studio and housing at low cost; confirm current terms.
residencies.disciplines: Craft media — clay, glass, metals, textiles, wood
residencies.summary: A long-term residency in the Blue Ridge Mountains giving craft artists several years to develop a studio practice.
residencies.applicationNote: Applications open periodically for multi-year resident places.

artistNeeds.point: Artists receive no share of resale appreciation in the US
artistNeeds.detail: There is no federal resale royalty, so an artist earns nothing when a work they sold cheaply later resells for far more. California's 1976 Resale Royalty Act was held preempted by federal copyright law for post-1978 sales in Close v. Sotheby's (9th Cir., 2018).

artistNeeds.point: Representation runs on introductions, not applications
artistNeeds.detail: Galleries overwhelmingly take on artists through referrals, studio visits and curator recommendations, and many state plainly that they do not review unsolicited submissions.

artistNeeds.point: Opportunities are scattered across hundreds of portals
artistNeeds.detail: There are more than 350 percent-for-art programmes in the US alone, each with its own registry and call process, and no shared index across them.

artistNeeds.point: Artists usually cannot see where their work goes
artistNeeds.detail: Once a work leaves the studio there is no standard mechanism telling the artist who owns it or what it later resold for, since dealer and private sale prices are typically confidential.

artistNeeds.point: Income is assembled from many small sources
artistNeeds.detail: Most artists sustain a practice through a mix of sales, grants, commissions, residencies and teaching rather than sales alone.

jurisdictionFacts.fact: The resale right splits sharply along jurisdictional lines
jurisdictionFacts.detail: An artist’s resale right is harmonised across the EU and exists in the UK and many other countries, but the United States — one of the largest art markets — has no federal equivalent. California’s 1976 Resale Royalty Act was held preempted by federal copyright law for post-1978 sales in Close v. Sotheby’s (9th Cir., 2018).

jurisdictionFacts.fact: Percent-for-art is the largest public commissioning stream in the US
jurisdictionFacts.detail: Philadelphia pioneered the model in 1959 and it has since grown to more than 350 programmes nationally, typically allocating between 0.5% and 2% of eligible capital budgets.
